source.title: Transform consistency for learning with noisy labels

record.tranche_reason: Reports test accuracy for a standard-training baseline across several noisy-label rates and describes its test-accuracy curve over training; it does not apply the original complete-random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Standard baseline test accuracy at several label-noise rates. It does not report training error, complete random labeling, fitting time, or shuffled-pixel/Gaussian-noise inputs. Other methods' results and cited findings are not rows for this claim.
record.test_reason: The Standard baseline supplies results on test-accuracy degradation under increasing random label corruption (V4). Its epoch curves also bear qualitatively on real-label learning preceding noise memorization (V6), as explicitly interpreted by the authors.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately reports the authors' interpretation of Standard's learning curves, but understates their main conclusion: transform consistency, small-loss selection, and combined hard and teacher-generated soft labels improve noisy-label classification, with claimed state-of-the-art performance on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Clothing1M.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a noisy-label training setup with symmetric or asymmetric corruption and reports test accuracy; it does not reproduce the complete-random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and label-noise type/rate change reported test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard test accuracy is 72.29% on CIFAR-10 and 30.08% on CIFAR-100 under the single asymmetric-noise condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard CNN generalization under structured, class-dependent label corruption.

record.problems: The relevant Standard baseline results give test accuracy but not training error. Symmetric corruption is tested at 20%, 50%, and 80%, not at none or all; asymmetric noise is a different corruption condition. Results are averages over the last 10 epochs, while the paper's epoch curves are not numerically reported in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results left out. Results for the proposed method and other baselines do not show what the claim's standard-training object does; the abstract and introduction's general statements are not independent result rows.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative fitting time and convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training-set fit, the uncorrupted and completely random endpoints, and smoothness between the three measured corruption rates.
Necessity or sufficiency of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation.
Direct, separate learning trajectories for clean and corrupted training labels; comparison with a completely random-label dataset.

missing.what: Qualitative Standard-baseline temporal result: test accuracy initially rises and subsequently declines. The authors explicitly attribute this to clean samples being learned before noisy samples. Record it separately from final test accuracy, with its indirect evidential status.
missing.locator: Section III.B.1, Figure 3 top and discussion; Section III.B.2, Figure 4 top and discussion

record.verdict_notes: Table values match the supplied text. Final test accuracy alone cannot establish memorization or perfect training fit. The proposed mitigation methods' performance does not establish failure of standard networks to fit random labels.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test complete random labeling or report training error and chance-level test error for it.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels, or convergence time across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Tests several noisy-label rates, but not the full range from none to all; does not report training-set fit or whether training error remains perfect.
No test of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation as regularization interventions.
Describes learning from noisy labels over epochs, but does not compare real labels with random labels or test whether they are learned differently.
